Surah An-Nur (The Light)

Medinan, and it has sixty-four verses (or sixty-two according to some counts).

﴿A surah which We have sent down and made obligatory⁠﴾ (the verb is read with a light or a heavy "f", the heavy form being because of the great number of obligations it contains). ﴿And We have sent down in it clear verses⁠﴾ (whose indications are evident), ﴿that you may remember⁠﴾ (read with the second "t" assimilated into the "dh", so that it is "tadhakkarūn"), i.e., that you may take heed and be admonished.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 24, verse 2:

﴿The adulteress and the adulterer﴾, i.e., those who are not *muhsan* (protected by marriage or free status), since stoning (*rajm*) for them is established by the Sunnah (the prophetic tradition). The *alif-lam* in *al-zaniyah* and *al-zani* as mentioned is a relative (*ism mawsul*, meaning "the one who"), and it is the subject (*mubtada'*). Because of its resemblance to a conditional (*shart*) construction, the particle *fa'* (then) entered its predicate, which is ﴿flog each one of them a hundred lashes﴾. *Jald* means a blow: *jaladahu* means he struck his skin (*jild*). The Sunnah adds to this a one-year exile (*taghrib*). For the slave, the punishment is half of what is mentioned.

﴿And let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of God﴾, i.e., in His ruling, by abandoning any part of their prescribed punishment. ﴿If you believe in God and the Last Day﴾, i.e., the Day of Resurrection. In this is an incitement toward what precedes the condition, and it is its answer, or it indicates its answer.

﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, i.e., the flogging. It has been said the group is three, and it has been said four, which is the number of witnesses required for adultery.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 3:

﴿The fornicator does not marry﴾ (yatazawwaj, marries) ﴿except a fornicatress or a polytheist, and the fornicatress—none marries her except a fornicator or a polytheist.﴾ That is, what is suitable for each of them is what has been mentioned. ﴿And that is forbidden﴾ — that is, marrying fornicators — ﴿to the believers,﴾ the righteous. This was revealed when the poor among the Emigrants (muhajirun) wanted to marry the prostitutes of the polytheists, who were wealthy, so that they would spend on them. It was said that the prohibition is specific to them, and it was said that it is general and was abrogated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And marry the unmarried among you﴾ (naskh, abrogation).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 4:

﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾ (al-muhsanat), of fornication, ﴿then do not produce four witnesses﴾ to their fornication, having seen it, ﴿flog them﴾, i.e., each one of them, ﴿eighty lashes, and never accept their testimony﴾ in anything ﴿ever. And those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun)﴾, for committing a major sin.

﴿Except those who repent after that and amend [their conduct]﴾, [for] ﴿indeed Allah is Forgiving﴾ to them for their slander, ﴿Merciful﴾ to them, by inspiring them with repentance (tawbah), through which their wickedness (fisq) ends and their testimony is accepted. It is also said that their testimony is not accepted. The exception (istithna') returns to the last clause.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 6:

﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ of adultery ﴿and have no witnesses except themselves﴾ to it. This happened to a group of the Companions. ﴿Then the testimony of one of them﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), ﴿four testimonies﴾ is put in the accusative as an absolute object (masdar), ﴿by Allah, that he is surely of the truthful﴾ regarding what he attributed to his wife of adultery.

Translation of the commentary on Qur'an 24:7:

﴿And the fifth [testimony is] that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is among the liars﴾ in that [accusation]. The predicate of the subject (khabar al-mubtada', the completing part of the nominal sentence): it averts from him the punishment for slander (hadd al-qadhf).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 8:

﴿And it averts﴾, i.e., it repels, ﴿from her the punishment﴾, the hadd (the fixed punishment) for fornication, which is established by his testimony, ﴿that she bear witness four times by Allah that he is surely among the liars﴾ in what he accused her of, namely fornication.
"And the fifth [testimony is] that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful" regarding that.

ÔI believe the request is to translate this passage. Here is the translation:

﴿And were it not for Allah's bounty upon you and His mercy﴾ by concealing [the matter] in this [case], ﴿and that Allah is Oft-Returning [to mercy]﴾ by accepting repentance in this and other [cases], ﴿Wise﴾ in what He decrees in this and other [cases], so that the truth in this [matter] is made clear, and He hastens the punishment upon whoever deserves it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 11:

﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander (al-ifk)﴾ the worst of lies against ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the Mother of the Believers, by slandering her, ﴿are a group among you﴾ a company of the believers, who were: Ḥassān ibn Thābit, ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy, Mistaḥ and Ḥamnah bint Jaḥsh. ﴿Do not consider it bad for you﴾ O believers, the group aside; ﴿rather, it is good for you﴾ Allah will reward you for it, and will manifest the innocence of ʿĀʾishah and of the one who came with her in this matter, who is Ṣafwān. For she said: "I was with the Prophet ﷺ on a military campaign after the veil had been revealed. When he had finished with it, he returned and drew near to Madinah, and he announced the departure one night. I walked and attended to my need, then I came back to the saddle, and suddenly my necklace (ʿiqd) had broken — it is with a kasrah on the unmarked letter, meaning the necklace (al-qilādah) — so I went back searching for it. Those who loaded my howdah (hawdaj) — which is what one rides in — onto my camel thought that I was in it, for the women were light; they only ate a small amount of food (ʿulqah), which is with a ḍammah on the unmarked letter and sukūn on the lām, meaning a little of the food. I found my necklace and came after they had set out, so I sat down in the place where I had been, thinking that the people would miss me and return to me. Then my eyes overcame me and I slept. Ṣafwān had halted behind the army, and he set out in the last part of the night for rest (idlāj), meaning he descended at the end of the night to rest, and he traveled on from there and arrived at his dwelling in the morning. He saw the dark shape of a sleeping person, meaning her figure, and he recognized me when he saw me, for he used to see me before the veil. I awoke at his saying of istirjāʿ when he recognized me, meaning his words, 'Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return.' I covered my face with my outer garment, meaning I veiled it with the cloth. By Allah, he did not speak a single word to me, nor did I hear from him any word other than his istirjāʿ, when he made his mount kneel and stepped on its forelegs, and I mounted it. He led the mount with me until we reached the army after they had halted in the heat of midday, meaning standing in a place of intense heat. Thereupon whoever was destroyed was destroyed, and the one who took the greatest part of it among them was ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl." End of quotation. Her narration is related by al-Shaykhān (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

﴿For every man among them﴾ meaning, upon him ﴿is what he has earned of sin﴾ in that matter; ﴿and the one who took the greatest part of it among them﴾ meaning, bore most of it, for he began to plunge into it and spread it, and he is ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy; ﴿for him is a great punishment﴾ which is the Fire in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 12:

﴿Why did you not﴾ (lawla) meaning "why not" (halla), ﴿when you heard it﴾ (idh) meaning "when" (hina), ﴿the believing men and believing women thought well of their own kind﴾, i.e., some of them thought well of others, ﴿and said, "This is a clear lie"﴾, a manifest falsehood. In it there is a shift (iltifat) from address: that is, "you thought, O company, and you said."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 13:

﴿Why did they not﴾ (lawlā: halla, "why not") ﴿bring﴾ (jā'ū) — i.e., the group — ﴿against him four witnesses﴾ (arba'ati shuhadā') — who witnessed it. ﴿Since they did not bring the witnesses, those, in the sight of Allah﴾ — i.e., in His judgment — ﴿they are the liars﴾ (al-kādhibūn) ﴿concerning it.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 14:

﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, you would have been touched, for what you plunged into, with a great punishment﴾ O company (al-'usbah), i.e., you engaged in (khudtum) ﴿in it, a great punishment﴾ in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 15:

﴿When you received it with your tongues⦆ — i.e., some of you narrate it from others. One of the two tā' (in the verb) has been elided. "Idh" (when) is in the accusative, governed either by "massakum" (touched you) or by "afadtum" (you plunged into).

﴿And you say with your mouths what you have no knowledge of, and you think it is trivial⦆ — that there is no sin in it — ﴿while it is, in the sight of Allah, grave⦆ — in terms of sin.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (*Tafsir al-Jalalayn*) on surah 24, verse 16:

﴿Why did you not﴾ (*halla*: "why not"), ﴿when﴾ (*hīna*: "at the time"), ﴿you heard it, you said﴾ ﴿it is not for us﴾ (*mā yanbaghī*: "it is not fitting"), ﴿to speak of this﴾. Here, "*hādhā*" (this) is for expressing wonder, ﴿This is a great slander﴾ (*kadhib*: "a lie").
﴿God admonishes you never to return to the like of it, ever again, if you are believers﴾ He forbids you ﴿to return to the like of it ever again, if you are believers﴾, so that you may heed that.
﴿And Allah makes the verses clear to you﴾ concerning the commands and prohibitions. ﴿And Allah is Knowing﴾ of what He commands and prohibits, ﴿Wise﴾ in it.

Indeed, those who love that indecency (al-fahisha) should spread among those who believe, by way of the tongue, by attributing it to them, and they are the group (al-usba) that spread the slander: ﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe﴾ will have a painful punishment in this world, by the legal penalty for slander (hadd al-qadhf), ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾ by the Fire, for the right of God. ﴿And God knows﴾ its absence from them, ﴿while you﴾ O group, by what you have said of the lie (al-ifk), ﴿do not know﴾ its existence among them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 20:

﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you﴾ O company [of slanderers] ﴿and His mercy, and that Allah is Kind and Merciful﴾ to you, ﴿He would have hastened upon you the punishment﴾

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 24, verse 21:**

﴿O you who have believed, do not follow the steps of Satan﴾: i.e., his paths of adornment (enticement). ﴿And whoever follows the steps of Satan - indeed, he commands indecency﴾: i.e., the follower; ﴿indecency﴾: i.e., the ugly deed, ﴿and wrongdoing﴾: that is, what is unlawful in the Sharia, by following them. ﴿And were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would have been purified, ever﴾: O you group (of slanderers), by what you said of the falsehood; ﴿not one of you would have been purified, ever﴾: i.e., would not have become righteous and cleansed of this sin through repentance from it. ﴿But Allah purifies whom He wills﴾: cleanses (them) from the sin by accepting their repentance from it. ﴿And Allah is Hearing﴾: of what you said; ﴿Knowing﴾: of what you intended.

﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear﴾ "the people of virtue" ﴿who are wealthy and well-off that they will﴾ "not give to the relatives, the needy, and the emigrants in the way of Allah" ﴿This was revealed about Abu Bakr, who swore that he would not spend on Mistah, who was the son of his maternal aunt, a needy emigrant (muhajir) who had fought at Badr (Badri), after Mistah had joined in the slander (al-ifk) against him, even though he had been spending on him. Some of the Companions (Sahabah) had also sworn that they would not give charity to anyone who had spoken anything of the slander﴾ "And let them pardon and overlook" ﴿them in this matter﴾ "Do you not love that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful" ﴿to the believers.﴾ Abu Bakr said: "Yes, I do love that Allah should forgive me," and he restored to Mistah what he used to spend on him.

Indeed, those who accuse ﴿chaste﴾ women, the virtuous ones, ﴿who are heedless﴾ of illicit acts, in that the thought of committing them never occurs to their hearts, ﴿believers﴾ in Allah and His Messenger, [they are cursed in this world and the Hereafter].

﴿The Day﴾. Its governing element (ناصبه, nāṣibuh) is al-istiqrār (السَّتْقرار, "being established"), the implied predicate attached to ﴿لهم﴾ (for them). ﴿Will testify﴾, read with the ta' above (التَّاء الفَوْقانيّة, al-tā' al-fawqāniyya), which is the form تَشْهَد, and with the ya' below (الياء التَّحْتانيّة, al-yā' al-taḥtāniyya), which is the form يَشْهَد. ﴿Against them, their tongues, their hands, and their feet, for what they used to do﴾, that is, of speech and of deed. And it is the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 25:

﴿On that Day, Allah will pay them their full recompense, the due they deserve﴾: He will repay them with the recompense that is owed to them. ﴿And they will know that Allah is the Truth, the Manifest﴾: when He fulfils for them the recompense about which they used to doubt. Among them was ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy. And "the chaste women" here refers to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ); no repentance is mentioned concerning the slander against them, whereas those mentioned in the slander against them at the beginning of Surat al-Tawba are others than them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 26:

﴿The evil women⟩ from among women, and ﴿the evil words⟩ [are for the evil men] from among people, ﴿and evil men⟩ from among people, ﴿are for evil women⟩ from what has been mentioned. ﴿And good women⟩ from what has been mentioned, ﴿are for good men⟩ from among people, ﴿and good men⟩ from among them, ﴿are for good women⟩ from what has been mentioned. That is, what is fitting for the evil is its like, and what is fitting for the good is its like. ﴿Those⟩ — the good men and the good women from among women, and among them ʿĀʾishah and Ṣafwān — ﴿are free from what they say⟩; that is, the evil men and the evil women from among men and women are the ones among them [who say it]. ﴿For them⟩ — for the good men and the good women — ﴿is forgiveness and a generous provision⟩ in Paradise. ʿĀʾishah took pride in several things, among them that she was created good and that she was promised forgiveness and a generous provision.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 27:

﴿O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own houses until you have asked permission [literally: until you seek intimacy/familiarity] and greeted their inhabitants﴾ — that is, ﴿tastaʼnisu﴾ means tastaʼdhinū (you seek permission), ﴿wa-tusallimū ʻalā ahlihā﴾ — so that the one [entering] says, "Peace be upon you, may I enter?" as has been reported in a hadith. ﴿That is better for you﴾ than entering without seeking permission, ﴿that you may remember﴾ — with the second tāʼ assimilated into the dhāl (in the reading of idghām), [meaning] its being better, so that you may act upon it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 28:

﴿And if you find no one therein, do not enter until permission is given to you. And if it is said to you, "Go back," then go back; it is purer for you;﴾ (i.e., the return) ﴿purer for you﴾ (i.e., better for you) than sitting at the door ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of what you do﴾ of entering with permission or without permission. ﴿He is All-Knowing﴾ and will recompense you for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 29:

﴿There is no blame upon you for entering houses not inhabited, wherein is provision﴾ i.e., benefit, ﴿for you﴾ by way of shelter and otherwise, such as the inns (rubut) and the public hostels (khanat al-musabbalah). ﴿And Allah knows what you reveal﴾ you make apparent ﴿and what you conceal﴾ you hide, in entering other than your own houses, whether with the intention of good or otherwise. And it will come that when they enter their houses they greet one another (lit. "greet themselves").

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 30:

﴿Say to the believing men that they should lower their gaze﴾ from what is not lawful for them to look at; and "min" (from) is extra. ﴿and guard their private parts﴾ from what is not lawful for them to do with them. ﴿That is purer﴾ i.e., better ﴿for them. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what they do﴾ with the eyes and the private parts, and He will recompense them for it.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 24, verse 31:**

﴿And tell the believing women to lower their gaze﴾ from what is not lawful for them to look at, ﴿and guard their private parts﴾ from what is not lawful for them to do with them, ﴿and not to display﴾ (yuzhirna, i.e., to show) ﴿their adornment, except what appears thereof﴾, which is the face and the two palms. So it is permissible for a non-mahram man to look at these if he is not afraid of temptation, according to one of two opinions. The second opinion holds that it is forbidden, because it is a likely cause of temptation, and this view was preferred as a means of closing the door (hasman lil-bab, i.e., blocking the means to harm). ﴿And let them draw their khumur (head coverings) over their juyub (chests/bosoms)﴾, meaning they should cover the heads, necks and chests with veils (maqani'). ﴿And not to display their adornment﴾, meaning the hidden adornment, which is everything other than the face and the two palms, ﴿except to their husbands﴾ (bu'ulatihinna, the plural of ba'l, meaning zawj, husband), ﴿or their fathers, or their husbands' fathers, or their sons, or their husbands' sons, or their brothers, or their brothers' sons, or their sisters' sons, or their women, or those whom their right hands possess﴾. For these people it is permissible for them to look, except at what lies between the navel and the knee, and it is forbidden for anyone other than husbands to look at that. The phrase "their women" excludes non-Muslim women, so it is not permissible for Muslim women to unveil before them. The phrase "those whom their right hands possess" includes male slaves. ﴿Or male attendants who have no physical desire﴾ among the men (ghayr is read in the genitive as an adjective and in the accusative as an exception), ﴿or children who have not yet become aware of women's private matters﴾ (al-tifl is understood in the sense of children), meaning those who have not come to know the intimate matters of women, for the purpose of intercourse. So it is permissible for women to reveal to them what lies outside the area between the navel and the knee. ﴿And let them not stamp their feet so as to reveal what they hide of their adornment﴾, such as an anklet that jingles. ﴿And turn to Allah in repentance together, O believers﴾ for what has befallen you of forbidden looking and other things, ﴿so that you may be successful﴾, meaning that you may be saved from that by the acceptance of repentance from you. In the verse, the masculine form predominates over the feminine.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 32:

﴿And marry off the unmarried (al-ayama) among you﴾ — plural of ayyim: one who has no spouse, whether a virgin or a previously married person, male or female. This applies to free people and free women.
﴿And the righteous among your male slaves and female slaves﴾ — the believers. ʿIbad is the plural of ʿabd.
﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them﴾ — i.e., the free ones — ﴿by His bounty﴾ through marriage. ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing﴾ in His provision for His creation, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of them.

﴿وَلْيَسْتَعْفِفِ الَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ نِكَاحًا﴾ ﴿And let those who cannot find the means of marriage﴾ — that is, the dowry and the maintenance with which they could marry — ﴿abstain﴾ from fornication (al-zina). ﴿حَتَّىٰ يُغْنِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ ﴿until God enriches them﴾ — He grants them abundance ﴿مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾ ﴿from His bounty﴾, so that they may marry. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يَبْتَغُونَ الْكِتَابَ﴾ ﴿And those who seek a writing﴾ — meaning mukatabah (a contract of manumission, by which a slave purchases his freedom in installments) ﴿مِمَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾ ﴿of those whom your right hands possess﴾ — from among the male and female slaves — ﴿فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ إِنْ عَلِمْتُمْ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًا﴾ ﴿then make a contract with them, if you know good in them﴾ — that is, trustworthiness and capacity to earn in order to pay the amount of the mukatabah. Its wording, for example, is: "I have made a mukatabah with you for two thousand over two months, a thousand each month; when you pay it, you are free," and he says, "I accept." ﴿وَآتُوهُمْ﴾ ﴿And give them﴾ — an imperative addressed to the masters — ﴿مِّن مَّالِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي آتَاكُمْ﴾ ﴿from the wealth of God which He has given you﴾ — that which they may use to fulfill what they have undertaken to you. The sense of "giving" (al-ita') includes remitting some part of what they have undertaken. ﴿وَلَا تُكْرِهُوا فَتَيَاتِكُمْ﴾ ﴿And do not compel your slave girls﴾ — your female slaves — ﴿عَلَى الْبِغَاءِ﴾ ﴿to prostitution﴾ — fornication (al-zina) ﴿إِنْ أَرَدْنَ تَحَصُّنًا﴾ ﴿if they desire chastity﴾ — abstaining from it. This desire is the very condition for compulsion, so the conditional clause has no implied opposite (mafhum al-shart). ﴿لِتَبْتَغُوا﴾ ﴿seeking﴾ by compulsion ﴿عَرَضَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ ﴿the goods of the worldly life﴾. It was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, who used to compel his slave girls to earn by fornication. ﴿وَمَن يُكْرِههُّنَّ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ مِن بَعْدِ إِكْرَاهِهِنَّ غَفُورٌ﴾ ﴿And whoever compels them, then indeed God, after their compulsion, is Forgiving﴾ to them ﴿رَّحِيمٌ﴾ ﴿Merciful﴾ toward them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 34:

﴿And We have certainly sent down to you verses clearly showing (the truth)﴾ — read with a fatha on the ya' (mubayyinat, "clarifying") and with a kasra on it (mubayyinat, "clear"); in this surah (it is) clarifying what has been mentioned in it, or (it is) a clear sign (bayyinah). ﴿And an example﴾ — a wondrous report, and it is the report of ʿĀʾishah ﴿of those who passed away before you﴾ — meaning, of the same kind as their examples, i.e., their wondrous reports, such as the report of Yūsuf (Joseph) and Maryam (Mary). ﴿And an admonition for the righteous﴾ — in His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿and let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah﴾; ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believers not think﴾ — etc.; ﴿and why, when you heard it, did you not say﴾ — etc.; ﴿Allah admonishes you never to return﴾ — etc. Its being specified for the righteous is because they are the ones who benefit from it.

﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., the One who illuminates them with the sun and the moon. ﴿The likeness of His light﴾, i.e., His attribute in the heart of the believer, ﴿is like a niche wherein is a lamp; the lamp is in a glass﴾. It is the qindil (lamp-stand), and the misbah (lamp) is the siraj (lantern), i.e., the wick that is kindled. The mishkat (niche) is a recess that does not pass through, i.e., the tube within the qindil. ﴿The glass, as if it were a star﴾, and the light is within it, ﴿a brilliant star﴾, i.e., shining. It is read as durri with a kasra on the dal and as durri with a damma on it. From the damma-form it derives from al-darʾ (repelling), meaning "pushing away," because it repels darkness. With a damma and a doubled ya', it is ascribed to al-durr, meaning pearls. ﴿It is lit﴾: the lamp (misbah) is read in the past tense, and in one qira'a (recitation, a variant reading) as the present form of awqada, in the passive with a ya' (yuqadu). In another reading it is tuqadu, with a ta' at the beginning, i.e., the glass is lit. ﴿From﴾ the oil of ﴿a blessed tree, an olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west﴾, but between them, so that neither a harmful heat nor a harmful cold reaches it. ﴿Its oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it﴾ because of its purity. ﴿Light upon light﴾: the light of the lamp by the fire, and the light of Allah, i.e., His guidance to the believer, is light upon the light of faith. ﴿Allah guides to His light﴾, i.e., the religion of Islam, ﴿whom He wills. And Allah strikes the parables for people﴾, explaining them, bringing them close to their understanding so that they may take heed and believe. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of everything﴾, and among that is His coining of parables.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 36:

﴿In houses﴾ related to "yusabbihu" that follows. ﴿Allah has permitted that they be raised﴾ that they be exalted. ﴿And that His name be mentioned therein﴾ by His Oneness. ﴿Glorified﴾ with the fatha and kasra of the letter ba' (i.e., yusabbihu, with the ba' read either with a fatha or a kasra): meaning, prays. ﴿To Him therein in the mornings﴾ a verbal noun in the sense of the plural "mornings": meaning the early hours. ﴿And the evenings﴾ the afternoons, from after the decline of the sun.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 37:

﴿Men﴾ is the subject (fa'il) of yusabbihu, read with a kasra on the ba'. On the reading with a fatha on it, it is the deputy subject (na'ib al-fa'il). ﴿Men﴾ is the subject of a verb understood (fi'l muqaddar), an answer to an implied question, as if it were said: "Who glorifies Him?" ﴿Neither trade nor sale distracts them﴾ from purchasing, ﴿from remembrance of God, the establishment of prayer﴾ with the ha' of iqamah (establishment) omitted, as a lightening, ﴿and the giving of zakat.﴾ ﴿They fear a Day when hearts and eyes will be turned about﴾ will be agitated ﴿within it,﴾ from the fear. The hearts are between salvation and destruction, and the eyes are between the two sides, right and left. It is the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 38:

﴿So that Allah may reward them with the best of what they did﴾ i.e., His reward; and "the best" (aḥsan) is in the sense of "good" (ḥasan). ﴿And increase them from His bounty. And Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾ It is said: "So-and-so spends without reckoning," i.e., he spends lavishly, as if he does not count what he spends.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 39:

﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level desert (qī'ah)﴾ — plural of qā' (a flat, open tract): i.e., in a wilderness, and it is a shimmer seen there at midday in the intensity of the heat, resembling flowing water. ﴿The thirsty one thinks it to be⦆ thinks it ﴿water⦆, i.e., the parched one, ﴿water, until when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾ of what he had supposed. Likewise the disbeliever thinks that his deed, like his truthfulness, will benefit him; until, when he dies and comes before his Lord, he finds that his deed is not (of any use), i.e., it did not benefit him. ﴿And he finds Allah with him﴾, i.e., with his deed, ﴿so He pays him his account in full﴾, i.e., He recompenses him for it in this world. ﴿And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾, i.e., in recompense.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 40:

﴿Or﴾ [the deeds of] those who disbelieve, their evil deeds, [are] ﴿like darknesses in a deep sea (lujji)﴾ deep, ﴿covered by a wave from above it﴾ — i.e., the wave: ﴿a wave from above it﴾ — i.e., the second wave; ﴿clouds﴾ — i.e., the cloud of this; ﴿darknesses, some above others﴾: the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the first wave, and the darkness of the second, and the darkness of the cloud. ﴿When he brings out﴾ the beholder ﴿his hand﴾ amid these darknesses, ﴿he almost does not see it﴾ — i.e., he does not come near to seeing it. ﴿And whomever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light﴾ — i.e., whomever Allah does not guide, he is not guided.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 41:

﴿Have you not seen that to Allah glorify whoever is in the heavens and the earth,﴾ and among the glorification is prayer, ﴿and the birds﴾ (plural of ṭā'ir, that which flies) between the sky and the earth, ﴿in ranks﴾ (ṣāffāt, a circumstantial state) spreading their wings. ﴿Each has known﴾ by Allah ﴿its prayer and its glorification, and Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾ In it is the predominance of the rational (taghlīb al-'āqil), i.e., the masculine rational plural form "man" (man) is used with the non-rational (the heavens, the earth and the birds), since the verse includes rational beings in the general reference.

To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ — the treasuries of rain, provision and vegetation — ﴿and to Allah is the final return﴾ — the return.

Note on the translation: the Qur'anic quotation is rendered in full within the ﴿ ﴾ markers, followed by the commentary's gloss. The passage above is the exact text supplied, so the first clause is the verse's own wording and the commentary's explanation follows the dash.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 43:

﴿Have you not seen that Allah drives the clouds gently﴾ (yasuquhu biriqq): drives it gently. ﴿then joins them together﴾ (yadummu ba'duhu ila ba'd): gathers some of it to some, making the scattered pieces one piece. ﴿then makes it into a heap﴾ (ba'duhu fawq ba'd): some of it upon other parts of it. ﴿and you see the rain﴾ (al-wadq): the rain ﴿coming out from its midst﴾ (makharijahu): from its openings. ﴿And He sends down from the sky mountains﴾ (min) in it is superfluous (za'ida), ﴿wherein is hail﴾ (fi al-sama'): in the sky, replacing the preposition by repeating it (bi-i'adat al-jarr), ﴿of hail﴾ (min barad): meaning some of it. ﴿So He strikes with it whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills.﴾ ﴿The brilliance of its lightning nearly﴾ (yakadu): comes close to ﴿taking away the sight﴾ (al-absar al-nadhira lahu): i.e., snatches away the eyes of those who look at it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 44:

﴿Allah alternates the night and the day﴾, i.e., He brings each of them in place of the other. ﴿Indeed in that﴾ alternation ﴿is a lesson﴾, a proof ﴿for those of insight﴾, for the people of discernment, of Allah's power, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 45:

﴿And Allah created every creature﴾, i.e., every animal, ﴿from water﴾, i.e., a drop of semen. ﴿Of them are some that walk on their bellies﴾, like snakes and creeping things, ﴿and of them are some that walk on two legs﴾, like humans and birds, ﴿and of them are some that walk on four﴾, like beasts and livestock.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 46:

﴿We have certainly sent down distinct verses﴾ i.e., clear proofs, which are the Qur'an, ﴿and Allah guides whom He wills to a path﴾ i.e., a way, ﴿straight﴾ i.e., the religion of Islam.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 47:

﴿And they say﴾ the hypocrites, ﴿"We believed﴾ we affirmed as true ﴿in Allah﴾ in His oneness, ﴿and in the Messenger﴾ Muhammad, ﴿and we obeyed"﴾ and we obeyed them both in what they judged ﴿Then a faction of them turns away﴾ turns aside, ﴿after that﴾ from it ﴿And those are not ﴾ the ones who turn away ﴿believers﴾ the known believers, whose hearts agree with their tongues.
And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger (the one who conveys from Him) so that he may judge between them, behold, a party of them turn away (from coming to him).
And if the right is theirs, they come to him willingly ﴿mudh'ineen﴾ — hastening, obedient.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 50:

﴿Is there in their hearts a disease﴾ (i.e., disbelief), ﴿or have they come to doubt﴾, i.e., they doubted His prophethood, ﴿or do they fear that Allah will be unjust to them, and His Messenger?﴾ in the judgment, i.e., that they would be wronged in it? No. ﴿Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers﴾ by turning away from it.

﴿The saying of the believers, when they are called to God and His Messenger so that He may judge between them, is only that they say: "We hear and we obey."﴾ So the fitting saying for them is ﴿that they say "We hear and we obey"﴾ by responding (affirmatively). ﴿And those, at that time, are the successful﴾, the ones who are saved.

﴿Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, and fears Allah﴾ means fears Him, ﴿and is mindful of Him﴾, with the ha in ﴿ويَتَّقْهِ﴾ read either with sukun, as ﴿ويَتَّقْهْ﴾, or with kasra, as ﴿ويَتَّقْهِ﴾, by obeying Him, ﴿those are the ones who are triumphant﴾ with Paradise.

And they swore by Allah with the utmost of their oaths, ﴿that if you ordered them, they would surely go forth.﴾ Say to them: ﴿Do not swear. Known obedience﴾ to the Prophet is ﴿better than your oath,﴾ which you are not truthful in. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do,﴾ of your obedience in words and your opposition in deeds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 54:

﴿Say: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away﴾ from his obedience, with one of the two taa' elided, the address being to them, ﴿then upon him is only what he has been charged with﴾ of conveyance (al-tabligh), ﴿and upon you is what you have been charged with﴾ of obeying him, ﴿and if you obey him, you will be guided. And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾ i.e., the clear conveyance (al-tabligh al-bayyin).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 55:

﴿God has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors in the land﴾, in place of the disbelievers, ﴿just as He made successors those before them﴾ (the verb being in the active and passive forms), ﴿those before them﴾ from the Children of Israel, in place of the tyrants. ﴿And He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them﴾, namely Islam, by making it manifest over all other religions and by widening their domain in the lands so that they possess them. ﴿And He will surely change [their state] after their fear﴾ (read with the lightening and the intensifying of the consonant), ﴿from the disbelievers﴾, ﴿into security﴾. God has indeed fulfilled His promise to them with what has been mentioned, and He praised them: ﴿They worship Me, not associating anything with Me﴾. This is a resumptive clause in the sense of a causal explanation. ﴿But whoever disbelieves after that﴾, after this blessing from Him, ﴿those are the defiantly disobedient﴾. The first to disbelieve in it were the murderers of ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, for they began to fight one another after having been brothers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 56:

﴿And establish the prayer, and give the zakat, and obey the Messenger, that you may be shown mercy﴾ — i.e., in hope of receiving mercy.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 57:

﴿Let not﴾ (read with the taa' above the line, or with the yaa' below it, the subject being the Messenger) ﴿those who disbelieve suppose they can escape [Us]﴾ (mu'jizeen) ﴿in the earth﴾, by eluding Us, ﴿and their refuge﴾ their place of return ﴿is the Fire; and wretched is the destination﴾ the place of return ﴿it is﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 58:

﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess [i.e., slaves, male and female] and those among you who have not reached puberty [i.e., of the free] ask permission of you [before entering] three times: before the dawn prayer, and when you put your clothing aside at midday [i.e., at the time of noon], and after the night prayer. Three times of nakedness for you.﴾ The word ʿawrāt (nakedness) is in the nominative (rafʿ) as the predicate (khabar) of an implied subject (mubtadaʾ) after which there is a genitive construction (muḍāf), and the muḍāf ilayhi has taken its place; i.e., these are times of nakedness. It is in the accusative (naṣb) by supposing an implied "times" (awqāt) in the accusative, as a substitute (badal) for the position of what precedes it, with the muḍāf ilayhi having taken its place. These are times for removing clothing, when nakedness becomes apparent. ﴿There is no sin upon you or upon them [i.e., the slaves and the children]﴾ regarding entering upon you without permission ﴿after these [three times]﴾, i.e., after the three times, they ﴿go about [attending] you [for service]﴾ ﴿some of you [being attendants] to others﴾. The sentence is an emphasis (taʾkīd) of what precedes it. ﴿Thus﴾, as what has been mentioned has been made clear, ﴿Allah makes clear to you the verses﴾, i.e., the rulings. ﴿And Allah is Knowing﴾ of the affairs of His creation, ﴿Wise﴾ in what He has arranged for them. It has been said that the verse of seeking permission is abrogated (mansūkha), and it has been said that it is not, but people have been negligent in abandoning seeking permission.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 59:

﴿And when the children among you reach puberty﴾, O free ones, ﴿let them ask permission﴾ at all times, ﴿as those before them asked permission﴾, i.e., the free adults.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 60:

﴿And as for women past child-bearing, who have no hope of marriage﴾ — they have ceased from menstruation and childbearing due to their old age. ﴿there is no blame upon them if they put off their outer garments﴾ — such as the jilbab, the rida' (cloak) and the qina' (veil) worn over the khimar; ﴿without displaying adornment﴾ — i.e., showing it openly, meaning hidden adornment such as a necklace, bracelet and anklet; ﴿but it is better for them to refrain﴾ — by not putting them off; ﴿and God is Hearing﴾ of your speech, ﴿Knowing﴾ of what is in your hearts.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 61:

﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor is there blame upon the lame, nor is there blame upon the sick﴾ in eating with those who are in their company, ﴿nor﴾ is there blame ﴿upon yourselves that you eat from your houses﴾, the houses of your children, ﴿or the houses of your fathers, or the houses of your mothers, or the houses of your brothers, or the houses of your sisters, or the houses of your paternal uncles, or the houses of your paternal aunts, or the houses of your maternal uncles, or the houses of your maternal aunts, or from that whose keys you possess﴾ that you have stored for others, ﴿or your friend﴾, who is one who is sincere to you in his affection. The meaning is that it is permissible to eat from the houses of those mentioned, even if they are not present, when it is known that they are content with it. ﴿There is no blame upon you that you eat together﴾, gathered together, ﴿or separately﴾, dispersed. (The word "ashtat" is the plural of "shatt", and it was revealed concerning those who were scrupulous about eating alone, and if they did not find anyone to eat with, they would leave off eating.) ﴿So when you enter houses﴾ that belong to you, with no people in them, ﴿then greet one another﴾; say, "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God," for the angels will return the greeting to you. If there are people in them, then greet them. ﴿A greeting﴾ (the word "tahiyyah" is a verbal noun from "hayya") ﴿from God, blessed and good﴾, for which you will be rewarded. ﴿Thus God makes the signs clear to you﴾, that is, He explains to you the landmarks of your religion, ﴿that you may understand﴾, so that you may comprehend that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 62:

﴿Truly, the believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, and when they are with him﴾ i.e., the Messenger, ﴿on a gathering matter﴾ such as the Friday sermon, ﴿they do not leave﴾ due to some excuse they have, ﴿until they seek his permission. Indeed, those who seek your permission, those are the ones who believe in Allah and His Messenger. So when they seek your permission for some of their affair﴾ i.e., their matter, ﴿then grant permission to whom you wish of them﴾ to depart.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 63:

﴿Do not make the calling of the Messenger among yourselves like your calling of one another﴾ by saying "O Muhammad!" Rather, say: "O Prophet of Allah! O Messenger of Allah!" with gentleness, humility and lowered voice. ﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away, sheltering behind one another﴾ i.e., they leave the mosque during the sermon without permission, secretly, concealing themselves behind something. Here "qad" is for emphasis (tahqiq). ﴿So let those who oppose his command beware lest a trial befall them﴾ i.e., of Allah and His Messenger, ﴿or a painful punishment afflict them﴾ in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 24, verse 64:

﴿Surely to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, (belongs to Him) in ownership, creation and servitude. ﴿He knows what you are upon﴾, O you who are responsible (for your actions), of faith and hypocrisy. ﴿And﴾ He knows ﴿the Day they are returned to Him﴾, where there is a shift (iltifat) from address (khitab) to third person, meaning, when it will occur, ﴿so He will inform them﴾ of it ﴿of what they did﴾ of good and evil. ﴿And Allah is Knower of all things﴾ of their deeds and other than them.
